title: Eviction policies: Redis as a cache against Redis as a database

videos.script: A Redis with no limit grows until the machine runs out of memory. {{limit}} Then the kernel kills the biggest process, and that is Redis. So you give it a ceiling, and a policy for what to do at the ceiling. {{policy}} The default policy refuses every new write. For a database, that is right. Nothing you stored disappears. {{refuse}} For a cache, it is wrong. The cache stops caching when it is busiest. {{cache}} The other policies delete keys to make room. They differ in which keys may go, and how one is chosen. {{grid}} You will run the same load under each one, and count what survived. {{load}} Then the instance that is a cache and a database at once. One policy refuses writes while its name says it evicts. Another quietly deletes records. {{mixed}} Last, expiry. A key whose time is up does not leave memory at that second, and you will watch the gap. {{expiry}}
